findings.title: `include_website_name` is missing the trailing `?` so the guard never runs
findings.body: ActiveModel::Serializers looks for a predicate named `include_<attribute>?`. The method is defined as `include_website_name` (no question mark), so it is dead code and `website_name` is unconditionally serialized. Consequences: (1) the key `website_name` is emitted with a `nil` value for every user that has no website, bloating every user payload and breaking any consumer that checks for key presence; (2) the intended `website.present?` gating is silently not applied. Rename to `include_website_name?`.

findings.title: `website_name` is not listed in `untrusted_attributes`, leaking a TL0 user's website to anonymous visitors
findings.body: `website` is declared in `untrusted_attributes` so that, when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true (TL0 user viewed anonymously), the URL is not exposed — this is an anti-spam/privacy measure. The new `website_name` attribute returns the website host (and, for same-domain sites, the full path) but is not added to `untrusted_attributes`, and its own include guard (see `include_website_name`) only checks `website.present?`. The restricted URL is therefore disclosed through `website_name`, defeating the existing restriction. Add `:website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` list (or make the include predicate also honour `scope.restrict_user_fields?`).

findings.title: `"." << website_host` mutates a string literal
findings.body: `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` uses destructive append on the literal `"."`. It happens to work today because each evaluation allocates a fresh literal, but it will raise `FrozenError` the moment this file gets `# frozen_string_literal: true` (or the interpreter is run with frozen literals enabled), and it is needlessly allocating/mutating. Use `".#{website_host}"` or `"." + website_host`.

findings.title: No spec covers `website_name` visibility, so the untrusted/include regressions are undetected
findings.body: The TL0-seen-as-anonymous context enumerates `untrusted_attributes` but does not include `website_name`, so the fact that the new attribute leaks a restricted website is not caught. There is likewise no spec for a user with a blank website (which currently serialises `website_name: nil` because the include predicate is misnamed `include_website_name`), nor for the sibling-subdomain branch (`www.example.com` website with `forum.example.com` instance). Add specs for these three cases so the guards are actually exercised.

findings.title: Domain-matching heuristic mis-handles `www.` hosts and false-positives on shared public suffixes
findings.body: The branch logic only compares hosts when the label counts are equal and > 2. Consequences: (a) website `http://www.example.com/user` on an instance hosted at `example.com` falls through to the `else` branch, where `"example.com".ends_with?(".www.example.com")` is false, so the path is dropped even though it is the same site — exactly the case this PR is meant to handle; (b) hosts sharing only a public suffix, e.g. website `foo.blogspot.com` with instance `bar.blogspot.com`, compare equal on the last two labels and get the full path rendered even though they are unrelated sites. Consider normalising a leading `www.` and comparing registrable domains instead of raw label suffixes.
